correctness.rationale: Each complete transversal yields n positive cyclic gaps summing to 2n; by positive integer majorization (n+1,1,...,1) is the unique minimum multiset and (2,...,2) is the unrestricted maximum. For n odd the latter exactly selects even or odd indices. For n even the all-2 vector violates the antipodal constraint, and every nonuniform vector majorizes (3,2,...,2,1). If its unique 1 and 3 are separated by k twos, antipodal parity requires k+1=n/2, forcing unique cyclic gap pattern. Strict discrete concavity makes these the only equality multisets. Chord f(g)=2R sin(πg/(2n)) is strictly concave and gives the stated sharp perimeter and penalty. Independently exhaustively enumerated all 2^n transversals for n=3,...,13 with exact f(g)=−g²: n≥3 minima 2n, odd maxima 2, even maxima 2n, and predicted energy values exactly. The finite checks are not substituted for majorization proof.
residual_risks: Only equally spaced points and strictly discrete concavity; weak concavity can produce additional equality cases.

value.rationale: Perimeter optimization for a complete antipodal transversal is a natural distinct quantity expressly posed in the earlier extremal-antipodal-polygon literature. The common strict-concavity majorization theorem gives exact extremizers and interpretable parity obstruction for an entire class of edge-local energies; the exact even-order perimeter deficit scales as π³R/(2n³). These exact classification/equality facts are not implied by the earlier area extremal patterns alone and are useful for geometric optimization.
residual_risks: The already known area configurations are credited, not counted as new; cannot claim unrestricted antipodal placements.

final_claim: For every n≥3, choose one endpoint from each opposite pair of 2n equally spaced circle vertices. Every strictly discretely concave integer gap cost Σ f(g) is minimized exactly by consecutive selections, maximized by two alternating selections when n odd, and by 2n rotations of the parity-forced 1,2,...,3,2,... pattern when n even; exact chord-perimeter formulas and cubic-even-order deficit follow.
limitations: Even-case equality pattern and all n quantified are proved analytically rather than inferred from exhaustive n≤13 checks.
Does not solve perimeter for arbitrary nonuniform antipodal positions.
